meaning: From Squalus: Latin squalus, “dirty” or “filthy” (squalid), an ancient name for marine fishes considered unfit for human consumption, including sharks; -formes “shaped like”
description: Mostly deep-water sharks with two dorsal fins, which often have a spine in front, and no anal fin. Spiny dogfish, gulper sharks, lanternsharks, sleeper sharks and kitefin sharks all belong here.
